copy.en:
How do farmers use river water for their crops?

Farmers take water from rivers to water their rice fields and vegetable gardens! This way of bringing water to crops is called irrigation.
copy.tl:
Paano ginagamit ng mga magsasaka ang tubig ng ilog para sa kanilang pananim?

Kumukuha ang mga magsasaka ng tubig mula sa ilog para idilig sa palayan at gulayan! Ang sistemang ito ng pagdadala ng tubig sa pananim ay tinatawag na irigasyon.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit sa mga mag-uuma sa tubig sa suba para sa ilang tanom?

Mokuha ang mga mag-uuma og tubig gikan sa suba aron ibisbis sa humayan ug tanaman! Kini nga paagi sa pagdala og tubig sa tanom gitawag og irigasyon.

copy.en:
How did people travel and move goods before roads were common?

People used rivers as paths for boats and rafts! They carried people and goods from one place to another right along the water.
copy.tl:
Paano nagbiyahe at nagdalhat ng mga produkto ang mga tao bago dumami ang kalsada?

Ginamit ng mga tao ang ilog bilang daanan ng bangka at balsa! Dito sila nagdalhat ng tao at mga produkto mula isang lugar papunta sa iba.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbiyahe ug pagdala og mga produkto ang mga tawo bisan wala pa modaghan ang mga karsada?

Gigamit sa mga tawo ang suba isip agianan sa sakayan ug balsa! Diri sila nagdala og mga tawo ug produkto gikan sa usa ka lugar ngadto sa lain.

copy.en: Road signs keep us safe! They tell drivers when to stop or slow down because fast vehicles are hard to stop quickly.
copy.tl: Tumutulong ang mga road sign na manatiling ligtas ang lahat! Sinasabi nito kung kailan huminto o magpabagal dahil mahirap pigilan ang mabilis na sasakyan.
copy.bis: Ang mga road sign motabang nga maluwas ang tanan! Magsulti kini kanus-a mohunong o mohinay kay lisod pahunongon ang paspas nga sakyanan.

copy.en:
Who first used the word 'cell'?

Robert Hooke did, in 1665! He looked at cork under a microscope and saw tiny empty spaces, which he named cells.
copy.tl:
Sino ang unang gumamit ng salitang 'cell'?

Si Robert Hooke, noong 1665! Nakita niya ang mga maliliit na puwang sa balat ng tapon sa ilalim ng mikroskopyo, at pinangalanan niya itong cell.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang unang migamit sa pulong nga 'cell'?

Si Robert Hooke, niadtong 1665! Nakita niya ang gagmayng bakanteng espasyo sa cork ilalom sa mikroskopyo, ug ginganlan niya kini og cell.

copy.en:
How do we know the age of sedimentary rock layers?

The lower layers are usually older than the ones on top! This helps us read the order of past life.
copy.tl:
Paano natin nalalaman ang edad ng mga patong ng sedimentary rock?

Kadalasang mas matanda ang nasa ilalim kaysa sa itaas! Dahil dito, nakikita natin ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng buhay noong nakaraan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsayod sa edad sa mga patong sa sedimentary rock?

Kasagaran mas tigulang ang naa sa ubos kaysa sa ibabaw! Tungod niini, mabasa nato ang sunod-sunod sa kinabuhi kaniadto.

copy.en:
Why do rock layers have different colors?

The color comes from minerals inside! Red has rusted iron, black has carbon from old plants, and white is often limestone. Each color is a clue to what is inside!
copy.tl:
Bakit magkakaiba ang kulay ng mga patong ng bato?

Galing ito sa mga mineral! Pula ay may kinalawang na bakal, itim ay carbon mula sa lumang halaman, at puti ay batong-apog. Palatandaan ito ng laman!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lain-lain ang kolor sa mga patong sa bato?

Gikan kini sa mga mineral! Pula adunay gikalawang nga puthaw, itom adunay carbon gikan sa karaang tanom, ug puti kay limestone. Timailhan kini sa sulod!

copy.en: The Grand Canyon in America shows millions of years of Earth's history! The Colorado River slowly carved the land, exposing rock layers like pages of a giant book.
copy.tl: Ang Grand Canyon sa Amerika ay nagpapakita ng milyon-milyong taon ng kasaysayan ng Daigdig! Dahan-dahang inukit ng Ilog Colorado ang lupa, na nagpakita ng mga patong ng bato parang pahina ng libro.
copy.bis: Ang Grand Canyon sa Amerika nagpakita sa milyon-milyong katuigan sa kasaysayan sa Kalibutan! Hinay-hinay nga gikutkot sa Suba sa Colorado ang yuta, nagpakita sa mga patong sa bato sama sa panid sa libro.

copy.en:
Why are some rock layers thick and others thin?

It depends on how much sediment arrives and for how long! Lots of mud over a long time makes it thick. We cannot tell exact years from thickness alone.
copy.tl:
Bakit may makapal at manipis na patong ng bato?

Depende ito sa dami ng sediment at tagal! Maraming putik sa mahabang panahon ang nagpapakinis. Hindi natin masasabi ang tumpak na taon basta sa kapal lang.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga baga ang uban ug nipis ang uban nga patong?

Nagdepende kini sa kadaghan sa sediment ug tagal! Daghang lapok sa dugay nga panahon mopabaga. Dili nato masulti ang tukmang tuig pinaagi lang sa gibag-on.

What's the difference between a rock and a mineral?

A rock is made of one or more minerals joined together, while a mineral is a single natural substance!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng bato at mineral?

Ang bato ay gawa sa isa o higit pang mineral na pinagsama-sama, habang ang mineral ay iisang natural na sangkap!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa bato ug mineral?

Ang bato hinimo sa usa o daghang mineral nga gisagol, samtang ang mineral usa lamang ka natural nga sustansya!

copy.bis: Ang matag bato adunay mga sikreto nga timaan! Gibasa sa mga siyentista ang mga mineral, init, ug puwersa sulod sa bato aron mahibaw-an ang nangagi sa Yuta.

copy.en:
Did you know some rocks are older than the dinosaurs?

Many rocks are millions of years old! They act like nature's diary, recording Earth's long history.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na ang ilang bato ay mas matanda pa sa mga dinosaur?

Maraming bato ay milyon-milyong taong gulang! Sila ang parang talaan ng mahabang kasaysayan ng Earth.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka nga ang ubang bato mas tigulang pa sa mga dinosaur?

Daghang bato ang milyon-milyon ka tuig na ang edad! Sila nagsilbing rekord sa taas nga kasaysayan sa Yuta.

Why are the inner planets rocky?

Near the hot Sun, only metal and rock stayed solid! Far away in the cold, gas giants gathered lots of gas and ice.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabato ang mga inner planets?

Malapit sa mainit na Araw, metal at rock lang ang naging solid! Sa malayo at malamig, ang gas giants ay nakatipon ng gas at ice.
copy.bis:
Nganong batoon ang mga inner planets?

Duol sa init nga Adlaw, metal ug rock ra ang nagpabiling solid! Sa layo ug bugnaw, ang gas giants nakatigom og daghang gas ug ice.

copy.en:
How different are the atmospheres of rocky planets and gas giants?

Rocky planets have a thin atmosphere — thin on Earth, even thinner on Mars, and almost none on Mercury. Gas giants? They're almost entirely made of thick atmosphere!
copy.tl:
Gaano kaiba ang atmosphere ng batuhing planeta at gas giant?

Manipis lang ang atmosphere ng batuhing planeta — nipis sa Earth, mas nipis pa sa Mars, at halos wala sa Mercury. Sa gas giant? Halos buong planeta ay makapal na atmosphere!
copy.bis:
Unza ka lain ang atmosphere sa batoon nga planeta ug gas giant?

Nipis ra ang atmosphere sa batoon nga planeta — nipis sa Earth, mas nipis pa sa Mars, ug halos wala sa Mercury. Sa gas giant? Halos tibuok planeta gihimo sa baga nga atmosphere!

copy.bis: Mas baga ang rocky planets kaysa sa gas giants! Gaan kaayo ang Saturn nga molutaw sa daghang dagat, pero ang batoon nga Earth molunod!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Earth's rocky composition and contrasts with a gas giant, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or cover their features/composition. It only touches on a single planet's characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: With solid ground, water, and air, it’s the only planet with life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter

copy.en: Earth is our rocky home! With solid ground, water, and air, it’s the only planet with life. We couldn't live on a gas giant!
copy.tl: Ang Earth ang batuhing tahanan natin! May matigas na lupa, tubig, at hangin, kaya ito lang ang planetang may buhay. Hindi tayo pwedeng tumira sa gas giant!
copy.bis: Ang Earth ang atong batoon nga puy-anan! Adunay gahi nga yuta, tubig, ug hangin, mao nga dinhi ra ang kinabuhi. Dili ta puyong molungtad sa gas giant!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gas giants spin way faster than rocky planets! Jupiter, the biggest of all, completes one spin in just about 10 hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Jupiter's rotation speed and contrasts gas giants with rocky planets. The content is related to the solar system but does not directly support the competency's broad descriptive task.

copy.en: Gas giants spin way faster than rocky planets! Jupiter, the biggest of all, completes one spin in just about 10 hours — its day is much shorter than Earth's 24 hours.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis umikot ang mga gas giant kaysa sa batuhing planeta! Ang Jupiter, kahit pinakamalaki, umiikot nang isang beses sa loob lang ng mga 10 oras — mas maikli ang araw niya kaysa sa 24 oras ng Earth.
copy.bis: Mas paspas motuyok ang mga gas giant kaysa sa batoon nga planeta! Ang Jupiter, bisan og pinakadako, motuyok makausa sulod lang sa mga 10 ka oras — mas mubo ang adlaw niya kaysa sa 24 ka oras sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: front teeth that never stop growing, so they must gnaw constantly to keep them from getting too long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (front teeth) but focuses on their continuous growth and the need to gnaw to control length, not on their role in movement or gathering food as required by the competency.

copy.en: Rats and other rodents have front teeth that never stop growing, so they must gnaw constantly to keep them from getting too long.
copy.tl: Ang mga daga ay may pang-harap na ngipin na patuloy na tumutubo, kaya kailangan nilang ngumata palagi para hindi ito humaba nang sobra.
copy.bis: Ang mga ilaga adunay atubangan nga ngipon nga padayon nga motubo, busa kinahanglan sila mokitkit kanunay aron dili kini motaas og sobra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keep their teeth from growing too long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes teeth as an outer body part and their role in preventing overgrowth, but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. The stated function is unrelated to movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Rodents often gnaw on wood and other hard things to keep their teeth from growing too long.
copy.tl: Madalas ngumata ang mga daga sa kahoy at iba pang matigas na bagay upang mapanatiling maikli ang kanilang ngipin.
copy.bis: Kanunay nga mokitkit ang mga ilaga sa kahoy ug uban pang gahi nga butang aron mubo ang ilang ngipon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its teeth wear down a little — keeping them from growing too long!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth, an outer body part, but focuses on how gnawing prevents overgrowth, not on the role of body parts in moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

copy.en: Every time a rodent gnaws on something, its teeth wear down a little — keeping them from growing too long!
copy.tl: Sa tuwing ngumangata ang daga, naaagnas at naninipis ang ngipin nito — kaya hindi ito humahaba nang sobra!
copy.bis: Matag higayon nga mokitkit ang ilaga, nagasap-ad ang ngipon niini — mao nga dili kini motaas og sobra!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why are rodent front teeth orange?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rodent front teeth, an outer body part, but does not describe their role in moving or gathering food. It only explains the orange color from iron-hardened enamel, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because iron makes their enamel harder!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions iron, a metal, but only as a component of tooth enamel. It does not identify properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper.

copy.en:
Why are rodent front teeth orange?

Because iron makes their enamel harder! That's what gives many rodents' front teeth their orange color.
copy.tl:
Bakit kulay-kahel ang harapang ngipin ng daga?

Dahil may bakal (iron) na nagpapatigas ng enamel nito! Kaya kulay-kahel ang harapang ngipin ng maraming daga.
copy.bis:
Nganong kolor kahel ang atubangang ngipon sa ilaga?

Tungod kay may iron nga nagpagahi sa enamel niini! Mao nga kolor kahel ang atubangang ngipon sa daghang ilaga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a rabbit's or rodent's teeth grow crooked, a vet must trim them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth, an outer body part, but does not describe their role in movement or gathering food. copy.tl: Kapag hindi pantay ang ngipin ng kuneho o daga, kailangan itong iputol ng beterinaryo dahil hindi ito kusang naaagnas.
copy.bis: Kung dili tul-id ang ngipon sa kuneho o ilaga, kinahanglan kining putlon sa beterinaryo kay dili kini mahait sa kaugalingon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rodent's front tooth enamel is harder than the back
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses rodent teeth and their self-sharpening mechanism, but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor identify their role in movement or gathering food. assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable

copy.en: A rodent's front tooth enamel is harder than the back, so as it gnaws, the softer back wears faster — keeping its teeth sharp like a chisel!
copy.tl: Mas matigas ang enamel sa harap ng ngipin ng daga kaysa likod, kaya habang ito'y ngumangata, mas mabilis na nagagasgas ang likod — nananatili itong matalas parang pait!
copy.bis: Mas gahi ang enamel sa atubangan sa ngipon sa ilaga kaysa luyo, mao nga samtang nagakitkit kini, mas paspas magasgas ang luyo — nagpabilin kining hait sama sa pait!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rodent's upper and lower teeth must meet correctly while gnawing

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth, an animal body part, but focuses on how teeth wear down when they meet, not on the role of outer body parts in moving or gathering food as required by G3-L-4. It does not describe teeth as a tool for gathering food or movement.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feature of rodent teeth but does not explain how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It lacks any evolutionary or adaptive context and is not an example of adaptation from secondary sources.

copy.en: A rodent's upper and lower teeth must meet correctly while gnawing — that's what wears them down evenly.
copy.tl: Para mawasak nang maayos ang ngipin ng rodent, kailangang magkasalubong nang tama ang itaas at ibabang ngipin habang ito'y ngumangata.
copy.bis: Aron mahait og maayo ang ngipon sa rodent, kinahanglan magkita og tarong ang taas ug ubos nga ngipon samtang kini mokitkit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a rodent's front teeth keep growing for its whole life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a body part (teeth) but does not describe its role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a rodent's front teeth keep growing for its whole life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: Continuous tooth growth could be an adaptation, but the card does not describe how animals have changed to suit their environment or give an example like mimicry or camouflage. It only states a fact about growth.

copy.en:
Do a rat's teeth ever stop growing?

No — a rodent's front teeth keep growing for its whole life and never stop!
copy.tl:
Tumitigil ba ang paglaki ng ngipin ng daga?

Hindi! Ang ngipin ng mga daga ay patuloy na lumalaki habang sila ay nabubuhay at hindi tumitigil.
copy.bis:
Mohunong ba ang pagtubo sa ngipon sa ilaga?

Dili! Ang ngipon sa mga ilaga padayon nga modako sa tibuok nilang kinabuhi ug dili gyud mohunong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: watching the ground below for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)

copy.tl: Ang roller ay madalas na nakadapo sa mga kable o lantad na sanga habang minamatyagan ang lupa para sa makakain.
copy.bis: Ang roller kasagarang motugdon sa mga alambre o hawan nga sanga samtang nagbantay sa yuta alang sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a comfy room temperature is usually about 68 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a typical room temperature value. It does not explain the difference between heat and temperature, which is the core of G7-F-8. The mention of temperature is merely vocabulary overlap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a comfy room temperature is usually about 68 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an indoor comfort temperature, not a weather characteristic such as air temperature in the local environment. It does not help identify basic weather characteristics, so it does not directly support G4-E-4.

copy.en: In Fahrenheit, a comfy room temperature is usually about 68 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit (68–77°F)!
copy.tl: Sa Fahrenheit, ang komportableng temperatura ng kwarto ay karaniwang 68 hanggang 77 degrees Fahrenheit (68–77°F)!
copy.bis: Sa Fahrenheit, ang komportable nga temperatura sa kuwarto kasagaran 68 ngadto 77 degrees Fahrenheit (68–77°F)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the root grows downward first, then the shoot grows upward afterward

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions root and shoot but only states the order of emergence during germination; it does not describe why the root and shoot systems are important, which is the core of G4-L-2.

copy.en:
What grows first from a seed?

When a seed germinates, the root grows downward first, then the shoot grows upward afterward.
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang lumalabas sa binhi?

Kapag tumutubo ang binhi, unang lumalabas ang ugat pababa, pagkatapos ay sumusunod ang usbong paitaas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mouna motubo sa liso?

Kung motubo ang liso, ang gamot mouna paubos, dayon ang salingsing motubo paibabaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses roots as anchoring structures, but the competency requires identifying the role of roots (and leaves, stems) in getting water and nutrients from the soil. The card does not address water or nutrient uptake, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most plants do have roots to hold on
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots

copy.en:
Do all plants have roots to hold on?

Most plants do have roots to hold on, but some water plants float freely instead of digging deep into the ground!
copy.tl:
May ugat ba ang lahat ng halaman para humawak?

Karamihan ng halaman ay may ugat para humawak, pero may mga halaman sa tubig na lumulutang at hindi gaanong nakatusok sa lupa!
copy.bis:
Naa bay gamot ang tanang tanom aron mokupot?

Kasagaran sa tanom naay gamot aron mokupot, apan naay mga tanom sa tubig nga molutaw ug dili kaayo nakasaksak sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Roots have a harder time gripping loose, sandy soil than firm soil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but focuses on their anchoring role in different soils, not on their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil as required by G3-L-5.

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on root function (anchoring) but does not describe the root and shoot system as a whole or why they are important in the general sense required by G4-L-2.

copy.en: Roots have a harder time gripping loose, sandy soil than firm soil — so a plant in a sandy spot can tip over more easily in the wind.
copy.tl: Mas mahirap kumapit ang ugat sa maluwag o mabuhanging lupa kaysa sa matigas na lupa — kaya mas madaling matumba ang halaman doon kapag may hangin.
copy.bis: Mas lisod mokupot ang gamot sa luag o balason nga yuta kaysa sa gahi nga yuta — mao nga mas dali matumba ang tanom didto kung naa'y hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Roots need air in the soil too

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important in the sense of the competency. It focuses on a specific condition (too much water) rather than the general importance of the root system.

copy.en: Roots need air in the soil too — too much water can drown them and make them rot.
copy.tl: Kailangan din ng hangin ang ugat sa lupa — kung sobra ang tubig, maaari itong malunod at mabulok.
copy.bis: Nagkinahanglan usab og hangin ang gamot sa yuta — kon sobra ang tubig, mahimo kining malumos ug madunot.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not describe the root and shoot system or explain why they are important, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Roots are one of the main parts of a plant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names roots as a plant part and does not describe how plant organs work together as a transport system.

copy.en: Roots are one of the main parts of a plant, along with the stem, leaves, and flowers.
copy.tl: Ang ugat ay isa sa mga pangunahing bahagi ng halaman, kasama ang tangkay, dahon, at bulaklak.
copy.bis: Ang gamot usa sa mga nag-unang bahin sa tanom, uban sa punoan, dahon, ug bulak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The water pushes it up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car

copy.en:
How does a heavy RoRo ferry float?

It's a large steel ship! The water pushes it up, letting it carry vehicles across the sea.
copy.tl:
Paano lumulutang ang malaking RoRo ferry?

Ito ay malaking barkong bakal! Itinutulak ito pataas ng tubig, kaya nakakapagdala ng mga sasakyan tawid-dagat.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglutaw sa dako nga RoRo ferry?

Kini dako nga barkong puthaw! Gitulod kini pataas sa tubig, mao nga makadala ug mga sakyanan tabok sa dagat.

assignedReviews.reason: An intestinal worm is not tracing how food travels through the digestive tract.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ascaris, the large roundworm, is one of the most common intestinal worms found in children in the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: A common roundworm is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
What's one of the most common worms in kids?

Ascaris, the large roundworm, is one of the most common intestinal worms found in children in the Philippines.
copy.tl:
Alin ang isa sa pinakakaraniwang bulate sa mga bata?

Ang Ascaris, ang malaking bilog na bulate, ay isa sa pinakakaraniwang bulate sa bituka ng mga batang Pilipino.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang usa sa labing kasagarang bulate sa mga bata?

Ang Ascaris, ang dakong lingin nga bulate, maoy usa sa labing kasagarang bulate sa tinai sa mga batang Pilipino.

copy.tl: Ang mga kawad ng kuryente ay binabalutan ng goma o plastik. Protektahan tayo nito para hindi makuryente kapag hinawakan!
copy.bis: Ang mga kawad sa kuryente gibalotan og goma o plastik. Maprotektahan kita niini aron dili makuryente kung mahikap!

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about rubber's grip but does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it compare different surfaces or measure frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubber grips surfaces really well! That's why it's used on tires and shoes to stop slipping.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions material (rubber) and surface grip, but does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect movement in a general sense. It only gives a single example without explanation of the factors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubber grips surfaces really well! That's why it's used on tires and shoes to stop slipping.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies friction (grip prevents slipping) but does not demonstrate friction producing heat or investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction. It is a simple statement about rubber's grip, not an investigation of friction.

copy.en:
Why do tires and shoe soles use rubber?

Rubber grips surfaces really well! That's why it's used on tires and shoes to stop slipping.
copy.tl:
Bakit goma ang ginagamit sa gulong at suwelas ng sapatos?

Mahusay kumapit ang goma sa ibabaw! Kaya ginagamit sa gulong at sapatos para hindi madulas.
copy.bis:
Nganong goma ang gigamit sa ligid ug suwelas sa sapatos?

Ayaw hawakan sila samtang nakakonekta sa kuryente! Pataya ang power source kung luwas, tumawag ug tabang dayon, ug sugdi ang CPR kung dili moginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: these measures protect us from the Sun's light and heat reaching our bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains why sun safety tips are part of earth-and-space lessons; it does not describe any specific safety measures to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light. It mentions that measures protect us but provides no actionable safety tips.

copy.en:
Why are sun safety tips part of earth-and-space lessons?

Because these measures protect us from the Sun's light and heat reaching our bodies, not just about clothing fashion!
copy.tl:
Bakit ang sun safety tips ay nasa aralin sa earth-and-space?

Dahil pinoprotektahan tayo nito mula sa liwanag at init ng araw na umaabot sa atin, hindi lang ito tungkol sa clothing fashion!
copy.bis:
Nganong ang sun safety tips naa sa leksyon sa earth-and-space?

Tungod kay kini nagaprotekta kanato sa kahayag ug kainit sa adlaw nga moabot sa lawas, dili lang kini bahin sa clothing fashion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To calculate electricity cost, convert wattage to kilowatts (divide by 1000), multiply by hours used, then by the price per kWh.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how to compute electricity cost from wattage and usage time. It does not describe how high-voltage electricity is generated or distributed, nor the roles of substations or electric meters. The mention of kWh and price is only tangentially related to the electricity distribution topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A 1000-watt aircon running 8 hours uses 8 kWh!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that power is the rate of doing work
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses power (wattage) and time to compute energy consumption and cost, but it does not teach that power is the rate of doing work. The concept of power is used as a given quantity, not defined or explained in terms of work per time.

copy.en: To calculate electricity cost, convert wattage to kilowatts (divide by 1000), multiply by hours used, then by the price per kWh. A 1000-watt aircon running 8 hours uses 8 kWh!
copy.tl: Para sa gastos sa kuryente, i-convert ang wattage sa kilowatts (hatiin sa 1000), paramihin sa oras na ginamit, at sa presyo bawat kWh. Ang 1000-watt aircon na gumagana ng 8 oras ay gumagamit ng 8 kWh!
copy.bis: Para sa gastos sa kuryente, i-convert ang wattage sa kilowatts (bahinon sa 1000), paramihin sa oras nga gigamit, ug sa presyo matag kWh. Ang 1000-watt aircon nga nagdagan ug 8 oras naggamit ug 8 kWh!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A closed metal vehicle is a safe shelter from lightning!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about lightning safety in a car, not about identifying electricity as a flow of electrons or safe handling of electrical equipment. It mentions current but not electrons, and lightning protection is not the same as handling electricity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A closed metal vehicle is a safe shelter from lightning!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a safety precaution for extreme weather (lightning), but it does not involve examining a local weather chart or making interpretations about local weather. It only addresses one safety measure, not the competency's chart-interpretation component.

copy.en: A closed metal vehicle is a safe shelter from lightning! The metal shell acts as a Faraday cage, carrying the current around passengers to the ground, not through them.
copy.tl: Ang saradong metal na sasakyan ay ligtas na kanlungan mula sa kidlat! Ang metal shell ay kumikilos bilang Faraday cage, na nagdadala ng kuryente palibot sa mga pasahero papuntang lupa, hindi sa kanila.
copy.bis: Ang siradong metal nga sasakyan ligtas nga kanlungan gikan sa kidlat! Ang metal shell kumikilos ingon Faraday cage, nga nagdala sa kuryente palibot sa mga pasahero paingon sa yuta, dili kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metal reflects microwaves and creates sparks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions microwaves but does not compare wavelengths or frequencies of different electromagnetic waves. It only gives a safety fact about metal in a microwave, which is not direct instructional support for comparing EM wave properties.

copy.en:
Why should you never put metal inside a microwave?

Metal reflects microwaves and creates sparks that can start a fire and damage the oven.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi mo ilalagay ang metal sa loob ng microwave?

Ang metal ay sumasalubong sa microwaves at gumagawa ng sparks na pwedeng magpa-support ng apoy at masira ang oven.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili ka magbutang ug metal sa sulod sa microwave?

Ang metal nagbalik sa mga microwave ug naghimo ug sparks nga pwedeng magsunog ug makasira sa oven.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A multimeter measures voltage (V), current (A), and resistance (Ω).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states what a multimeter measures. It does not support the competency's core action of inferring the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits, nor does it involve guided investigations or circuit assembly. The shared vocabulary (voltage, current, resistance) is not enough for direct support.

copy.en: A multimeter measures voltage (V), current (A), and resistance (Ω). Electricians and students use it to test circuits and electrical components!
copy.tl: Ang multimeter ay sumusukat ng voltage (V), current (A), at resistance (Ω). Ginagamit ito ng mga electrician at students para i-test ang circuits!
copy.bis: Ang multimeter nagsukat sa voltage (V), current (A), ug resistance (Ω). Gigamit kini sa mga electrician ug students aron i-test ang mga circuit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never touch it! It may still be live and can kill.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a safety rule about fallen power lines but does not teach that electricity is a flow of electrons, which is a required part of the competency. The safety advice alone is only loosely related to the full competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never touch it! It may still be live and can kill.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a specific post-typhoon hazard (fallen power lines) rather than general safety precautions for household electrical devices. It does not describe or explain the need for safety precautions in handling household devices, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What should you do if you see a fallen power line after a typhoon?

Never touch it! It may still be live and can kill. Always call the electric company or local authorities to report it safely.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gagawin mo kung may makitang nahulog na linya ng kuryente pagkatapos ng bagyo?

Huwag hawakan! Maaari itong buhay pa at makakapatay. Tumawag agad sa electric company o lokal na awtoridad para iulat ito.
copy.bis:
Unsay imong buhaton kung makakita ka ug nahulog nga linya sa kuryente pagkahuman sa bagyo?

Ayaw hawakan! Mahimong buhay pa kini ug makapatay. Tumawag dayon sa electric company o lokal nga awtoridad aron ireport kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Appliances on standby use a small amount of electricity called 'standby power' or 'vampire power', which adds to your electricity bill!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to identify ways to reduce the use of electrical energy in Filipino houses and communities and explain what local and global benefits can be achieved
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that standby power adds to the electricity bill. It does not identify ways to reduce electrical energy use, nor does it explain local/global benefits, which are the actions in the competency. The fact is background that could support a discussion but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
Did you know your TV still uses power when it's turned off but plugged in?

Yes! Appliances on standby use a small amount of electricity called 'standby power' or 'vampire power', which adds to your electricity bill!
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na gumagamit pa rin ng kuryente ang TV mo kapag nakapatay pero naka-plug?

Oo! Ang mga appliance sa standby ay gumagamit ng maliit na kuryente na tinatawag na 'standby power' o 'vampire power', na nagdadagdag sa electric bill!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga nagagamit gihapon sa kuryente ang imong TV kung napatay apan naka-plug?

Oo! Ang mga appliance sa standby nagagamit ug gamay nga kuryente nga gitawag 'standby power' o 'vampire power', nagdugang sa electric bill!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: ground safely carries stray current to earth to protect you!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the function of the ground pin as a protective feature, but it does not describe or explain safety precautions for handling household electrical devices, such as unplugging, avoiding water, or proper handling procedures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A Philippine plug has three pins: (1) live carries 220 volts from the grid; (2) neutral returns current; and (3) ground safely carries stray current to earth to protect you!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies plug pins and mentions grounding for protection, but it does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons nor teach safe measures in handling electricity. It only touches on a safety-related feature without addressing the competency's core content.

copy.en: A Philippine plug has three pins: (1) live carries 220 volts from the grid; (2) neutral returns current; and (3) ground safely carries stray current to earth to protect you!
copy.tl: Ang Philippine plug ay may tatlong pin: (1) live nagdadala ng 220 volts mula sa grid; (2) neutral nagbabalik ng kuryente; at (3) ground nagdadala ng stray current sa lupa para protektahan ka!
copy.bis: Ang Philippine plug adunay tulo ka pin: (1) live nagdala sa 220 volts gikan sa grid; (2) neutral nagbalik sa kuryente; ug (3) ground luwas nagdala sa stray current sa yuta aron protektahan ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ohm's law (V = I × R) links voltage, current, and resistance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the Ohm's law relationship and gives a 220V outlet example, which is useful background for understanding current, voltage, and resistance. However, the competency specifically requires guided investigations inferring this relationship in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery; the card does not address circuits, series/parallel arrangements, or investigation procedures.

copy.en: Ohm's law (V = I × R) links voltage, current, and resistance. At a 220V outlet, 110 ohms of resistance means 2 amperes of current!
copy.tl: Ang Ohm's law (V = I × R) nag-uugnay sa voltage, current, at resistance. Sa 220V outlet, 110 ohms ng resistance ay 2 amperes ng current!
copy.bis: Ang Ohm's law (V = I × R) nag-uugnay sa voltage, current, ug resistance. Sa 220V outlet, 110 ohms sa resistance mao ang 2 amperes sa current!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The watt measures electrical power
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that power is the rate of doing work
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the watt as a unit of electrical power but never states that power is the rate of doing work (work/time). It shares the term 'power' but does not directly support the competency's concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one kilowatt equals 1,000 watts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains watt and kilowatt units and compares bulb/aircon power consumption. It does not describe generation, high-voltage transmission, distribution, substations, or electric meters, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The watt measures electrical power, and one kilowatt equals 1,000 watts! A 60-watt bulb uses much less power than a 1,500-watt aircon.
copy.tl: Ang watt ang yunit ng electrical power, at 1 kilowatt ay 1,000 watts! Ang 60-watt na bulb ay mas kaunti ang power kaysa 1,500-watt na aircon.
copy.bis: Ang watt mao ang yunit sa electrical power, ug 1 kilowatt katumbas sa 1,000 watts! Ang 60-watt nga bulb mas gamay og power kaysa 1,500-watt nga aircon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: karst limestone caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names limestone as a rock type in a specific location. It does not support observing/collecting different rock types or describing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: karst limestone caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a local landform (karst limestone caves) but does not describe how landforms influence living or non-living components of the environment, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: karst limestone caves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a non-living thing (limestone/rock) but does not support guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around school, nor does it describe their properties.

copy.en: Sagada in Mountain Province is famous for karst limestone caves like Lumiang and Sumaguing! It's also known for 'hanging coffins,' where ancestor coffins are attached right to the rocky mountain cliff walls!
copy.tl: Ang Sagada sa Mountain Province ay sikat sa mga karst limestone caves tulad ng Lumiang at Sumaguing! Kilala rin ito sa mga 'hanging coffins,' nakakabit sa mga batoong pader ng bundok!
copy.bis: Ang Sagada sa Mountain Province bantog sa karst limestone caves sama sa Lumiang ug Sumaguing! Bantog usab kini sa 'hanging coffins,' diin ang mga kabaon sa ninuno gikabit sa bato-bato nga mga pader sa bukid!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Male sailfin lizards usually flash brighter colors than females
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sexual dimorphism in coloration, not the outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and gathering food. It shares the animal topic but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Male sailfin lizards usually flash brighter colors than females, often showing vivid green and blue tones.
copy.tl: Karaniwang mas maliwanag ang kulay ng lalaking sailfin lizard kaysa babae, na may makikitang matingkad na berde at asul.
copy.bis: Kasagaran mas hayag ang kolor sa lalaking sailfin lizard kaysa babaye, nga adunay matingkad nga berde ug asul.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A male sailfin lizard's sail is much bigger and taller than a female's
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (the sail) but its stated role is to show off, attract a mate, and warn off rivals, not to move or gather food as required by G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: attract a mate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on reproduction indirectly through mate attraction, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as required by G3-L-3.

copy.en: A male sailfin lizard's sail is much bigger and taller than a female's — he uses it to show off, attract a mate, and warn off rival males.
copy.tl: Mas malaki at mas mataas ang layag ng lalaking sailfin lizard kaysa sa babae — ginagamit niya ito para magpasikat, makaakit ng kapareha, at takutin ang ibang lalaki.
copy.bis: Mas dako ug mas taas ang layag sa laki nga sailfin lizard kaysa sa baye — gigamit niya kini aron magpasundayag, makadani og kapikas, ug hadlokon ang laing laki.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the big sail-like fin along its back and tail
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (the sail-like fin) but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of G3-L-4. It only notes that it is a distinctive feature, largest in males.

copy.en:
Why is it called a 'sailfin' lizard?

The sailfin lizard gets its name from the big sail-like fin along its back and tail — biggest in males, and its most distinctive feature.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag na 'sailfin' ang butiking ito?

Ang sailfin lizard ay tinawag dahil sa malaking palikpik na parang layag sa likod at buntot nito — pinakamalaki sa mga lalaki at tanging kilalanin ng hayop na ito.
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag og 'sailfin' kining butikia?

Ang sailfin lizard gitawag tungod sa dako nga palikpik nga morag layag sa likod ug ikog niini — labing dako sa mga laki ug maoy pinaka-inila nga marka niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: most of that length is its long tail
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the tail as an outer body part but does not describe its role in movement or gathering food, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: can grow almost a meter long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the unit 'meter' but does not describe or demonstrate the science process skill of measuring; it merely states a length.

copy.en:
How much of a sailfin lizard is just tail?

More than half! A sailfin lizard can grow almost a meter long, and most of that length is its long tail.
copy.tl:
Gaano karami ang buntot sa katawan ng sailfin lizard?

Mahigit kalahati! Umaabot ang sailfin lizard ng halos isang metro ang haba, at karamihan nito ay ang mahaba niyang buntot.
copy.bis:
Pila ka bahin sa lawas sa sailfin lizard ang ikog ra?

Kapin sa katunga! Moabot ang sailfin lizard og hapit usa ka metro ang gitas-on, ug kadaghanan niini mao ang taas nga ikog niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: On top of a sailfin lizard's head is a tiny light-sensing spot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (a light-sensing spot on the head), but its stated role is sensing light to tell day from night, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it helps the lizard tell day from night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies a response to light, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The response to light is not framed as a characteristic of living things, and the card does not teach the competency's content.

copy.en:
Does a lizard have a third eye?

On top of a sailfin lizard's head is a tiny light-sensing spot. It can't see pictures, but it helps the lizard tell day from night.
copy.tl:
May third eye ba ang butiki?

Sa tuktok ng ulo ng sailfin lizard ay may maliit na bahaging nakakaramdam ng liwanag. Hindi ito nakakakita ng larawan, pero nakakatulong ito para malaman kung araw o gabi na.
copy.bis:
Naa bay ikatulo nga mata ang lagarto?

Sa tumoy sa ulo sa sailfin lizard adunay gamay nga bahin nga makabati og kahayag. Dili kini makakita og hulagway, apan makatabang kini aron mahibaw-an kon adlaw o gabii na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A special bud of cells called a blastema forms right at the wound — and amazingly, it grows into a brand-new leg!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes regeneration of a salamander leg via a blastema, which is an example of growth and repair, but it does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the two types of cell division. It provides no direct instructional support for recognizing the two types of cell division or describing mitosis as cell division for growth and repair.

copy.en:
How does a salamander regrow a lost leg?

A special bud of cells called a blastema forms right at the wound — and amazingly, it grows into a brand-new leg!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakatubo ng bagong paa ang salamander?

May bumubuong espesyal na umbok ng selula na tinatawag na blastema sa sugat — at ito mismo ang nagiging bagong paa!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtubo pag-usab sa tiil sa salamander?

May motubo nga espesyal nga umbok sa selula nga gitawag blastema diha mismo sa samad — ug kini ang mahimong bag-ong tiil!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: iodine added to help with proper growth and a healthy thyroid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iodine as a nutrient for growth and thyroid health, but does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or how living things depend on the environment to meet those needs. The mention of growth is not tied to the concept of basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: iodine added to help with proper growth and a healthy thyroid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth as a benefit of iodine, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It does not teach that living things grow, respond, or reproduce; it only references growth in a nutritional context.

copy.en:
Why do stores in the Philippines sell iodized salt instead of regular salt?

Most salt in the Philippines has iodine added to help with proper growth and a healthy thyroid in your neck! It was added so everyone gets it, even far from the sea.
copy.tl:
Bakit karamihan sa asin na binibili sa Pilipinas ay iodized o may dagdag na yodo?

Idinagdag ang yodo sa asin para tumulong sa wastong paglaki at kalusugan ng thyroid sa leeg mo! Ginawa ito para makuha ng lahat ang yodo, kahit malayo sa dagat.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kadaghanan sa asin nga gipalit sa Pilipinas naay dugang nga yodo (iodized)?

Gidugang ang yodo sa asin aron motabang sa hustong pagtubo ug kahimsog sa thyroid sa imong liog! Gihimo kini aron makakuha ang tanan, bisan pa layo sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your muscles need the right amount of salt to move smoothly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a factor affecting muscle function (salt) and a symptom (cramps), but it does not describe how the muscular system works (e.g., contraction, movement, or the system's role). It is only tangentially related to the muscular system.

copy.en:
Why do your muscles get painful cramps after playing for a long time?

Your muscles need the right amount of salt to move smoothly! When you sweat a lot without drinking, salt runs low and causes cramps, so always rest and drink water.
copy.tl:
Bakit nangungulang o nagsusumpong ng cramps ang kalamnan mo pagkatapos maglaro nang matagal?

Kailangan ng kalamnan mo ng tamang dami ng asin para gumalaw nang maayos! Kapag sobrang pawis at hindi nakainom, nangungulang ang asin kaya nagiging pulikat, kaya magpahinga at uminom.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga nagsusumpong og pulikat ang imong mga kaunoran pagkahuman og dugay nga pagdula?

Ang imong mga kaunoran nagkinahanglan ug husto nga asin aron molihok og maayo! Kung maghinging-singot ug dili moinom, makulang ang asin ug mao ang hinungdan sa pulikat, mao nga importante nga mopahuway ug moinom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a mix of a little salt and sugar in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a solution (salt and sugar in water) but does not identify which component is the solute and which is the solvent, nor explain their roles. It only describes the mixture as a remedy, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a mix of a little salt and sugar in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a solution (ORS) but does not describe it as a uniform mixture, contrast it with non-uniform mixtures, or mention suspensions. It lacks the instructional content needed to describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

copy.en: When someone has diarrhea, the body loses water and salt. That's why there's oral rehydration solution (ORS)—a mix of a little salt and sugar in water to help the body recover fast!
copy.tl: Kapag may pagtatae, nawawala ang tubig at asin ng katawan. Kaya may inumin na oresol—halong kaunting asin at asukal sa tubig—para mabilis mabawi ang nawala!
copy.bis: Kung adunay pagtatae, mawala ang tubig ug asin sa lawas. Mao nga adunay ilimnon nga oresol—gisagol nga gamay nga asin ug asukal sa tubig—aron dali makabawi ang nawala!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It slows down the bacteria that make food rot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains salt slows bacterial growth, a biological spoilage mechanism, not a factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction. Food preservation is mentioned in the competency, but the card does not address chemical reaction rates (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area) or how they apply to preservation.

copy.en:
Why do we use salt to preserve food like dried fish?

Salt doesn't just add flavor—it keeps food from spoiling! It slows down the bacteria that make food rot. That's why Filipinos have been making dried fish and fish paste for a long time!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginagamit ang asin para i-preserve ang pagkain tulad ng tuyo?

Hindi lang pampalasa ang asin—pinipigilan nito ang pagkabulok! Pinipigilan nito ang pagdami ng bakterya na nagpapabulok ng pagkain. Kaya matagal nang ginagawa ng mga Pilipino ang tuyo at bagoong!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga gigamit ang asin aron i-preserve ang pagkaon sama sa bulad?

Dili lang pampalami ang asin—makapahinay kini sa pagkadunot! Makapahinay kini sa pagdaghan sa mga bakterya nga makapadunot sa pagkaon. Mao nga dugay na nga ginahimo sa mga Pilipino ang bulad ug ginamos!

copy.tl: Kapag pinapawisan ka, lumalabas ang tubig at kaunting asin sa katawan mo! Kaya maalat ang pawis. Kailangan mong uminom at kumain pagkatapos maglaro para mapalitan ang nawala.
copy.bis: Kung magsingot ka, mogawas ang tubig ug gamay nga asin sa imong lawas! Mao nga parat ang singot. Kinahanglan ka moinom ug mokaon human magdula aron mapuli ang nawala.

copy.en: Your body needs salt, but too much makes your heart and kidneys work harder and leaves you very thirsty! The right amount is always best—not too little and not too much.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng katawan mo ng asin, pero ang sobra ay nagpapahirap sa puso at mga bato mo at nagpapauhaw! Kaya tama lang na asin ang dapat—hindi kulang, hindi sobra.
copy.bis: Ang lawas nagkinahanglan ug asin, apan ang sobra nagpapalalis sa imong kasingkasing ug mga kidney ug nagpauhaw! Mao nga ang husto ra nga asin ang maayo—dili kulang, dili sobra.

copy.en: Salt acts like a water manager inside your body, keeping the right amount of water inside and outside your cells! If the balance gets upset, it makes you thirsty or puffy.
copy.tl: Ang asin ay parang tagapamahala ng tubig sa katawan mo, pinapanatili nito ang tamang dami ng tubig sa loob at labas ng mga selula! Kapag nagulo ang balanse, nauuhaw o namamaga ka.
copy.bis: Ang asin murag tigdumala sa tubig sulod sa imong lawas, nagpabilin kini sa husto nga tubig sulod ug gawas sa mga selula! Kung magubot ang balanse, mahimo kang uhawon o manghupong.

copy.tl: Nagdaragdag ng masarap na lasa ang asin sa pagkain! Pero kaunti lang ang sapat — kapag sobra, masyadong maalat ang ulam!
copy.bis: Nagadugang og lami ang asin sa pagkaon! Apan gamay lang ang igo — kung sobra, sobra ka parat ang sud-an!

copy.en:
Does all salt come from the ocean?

Nope! Salt also comes from the ground as rock salt dug from deep mines!
copy.tl:
Mula ba sa dagat ang lahat ng asin?

Hindi lang! Maaari rin itong kunin sa lupa bilang rock salt na hinuhukay sa mga mina!
copy.bis:
Gikan ba sa dagat ang tanang asin?

Dili lang! Makuha usab kini gikan sa yuta isip rock salt nga kaluton sa mga minahan!

copy.bis: Kinahanglan natong kaonon ang asin ug lana sa kasarangan lamang. Ang sobra makadaot sa kasingkasing ug makapataas sa presyon sa dugo!

copy.en:
How does salt keep food from spoiling?

Through osmosis! Salt's high concentration draws water out of bacteria and food cells, making it really hard for bacteria to survive and grow.
copy.tl:
Paano pinapanatili ng asin ang pagkain na hindi mapanis?

Sa pamamagitan ng osmosis! Kinukuha ng mataas na konsentrasyon ng asin ang tubig mula sa bacteria at food cells, kaya hirap silang mabuhay at lumaki.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpreserba sa asin sa pagkain aron dili madungog?

Pinaagi sa osmosis! Ang taas nga konsentrasyon sa asin nagkuha og tubig gikan sa bacteria ug food cells, lisud kaayo para sa bacteria nga mabuhay ug motubo.

copy.en: Besides seasoning, salt keeps food from spoiling, like in our yummy dried and salted fish!
copy.tl: Bukod sa pagtimpla, ginagamit din ang asin para hindi masira ang pagkain tulad ng tuyo at daing!
copy.bis: Gawas sa pagtimpla, gigamit usab ang asin aron dili madunot ang pagkaon sama sa bulad nga isda!

copy.en: Salt stops spoiling because it pulls water out of tiny germs (bacteria)! Without water, the germs that rot food simply cannot grow.
copy.tl: Pumipigil ang asin sa pagkabulok dahil hinihigop nito ang tubig palabas ng maliliit na kagaw (bacteria)! Kapag walang tubig, hindi makalago ang mga kagaw na sumisira ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang asin makapugong sa pagkadunot tungod kay gisuyop niini ang tubig pagawas sa gagmay nga kagaw (bacteria)! Kung walay tubig, dili makatubo ang mga kagaw nga maoy modaot sa pagkaon.

copy.en:
Is too much salt bad for us?

We need salt, but too much can harm our heart and blood pressure!
copy.tl:
Masama ba ang sobrang asin sa atin?

Kailangan natin ng asin, pero sobrang dami ay makasama sa puso at presyon ng dugo!
copy.bis:
Dili ba maayo ang sobrang asin para kanato?

Kinahanglan nato ang asin, pero ang sobra makadaot sa atong kasingkasing ug presyon sa dugo!

copy.tl: Maalat ang lasa ng tuyo at ibang inasnan na pagkain dahil maraming asin ang ginamit para i-preserve!
copy.bis: Parat kaayo ang lami sa bulad ug uban pang giasinan nga pagkaon kay daghan og asin nga gigamit aron tipigan!

copy.en:
How does salt keep food from spoiling?

Salt pulls water out of the food and out of the microbes! Without water, the microbes cannot easily grow.
copy.tl:
Paano pinipigilan ng asin ang pagkasira ng pagkain?

Humahatak ang asin ng tubig palabas ng pagkain at ng mga mikrobyo! Kaya hindi sila madaling makadami.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpugong sa asin sa pagkadunot sa pagkaon?

Mokuha ang asin sa tubig gikan sa pagkaon ug gikan sa mga mikrobyo! Mao nga dili sila dali modaghan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food preservation via salting and drying, but does not explain any factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area). It only states a preservation method without linking it to reaction rates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meat can be preserved by salting and drying it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a preservation method but does not demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restricting burning or handling reactive materials. Salting/drying is not about minimizing harmful changes in materials in the sense of the competency.

copy.en:
Can meat last a long time without a fridge?

Yes! Meat can be preserved by salting and drying it, just like tapa! That's how it stays good for a much longer time.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang tumagal ang karne nang matagal nang walang refrigerator?

Oo! Maaaring iimbak ang karne sa pamamagitan ng pag-aasin at pagpapatuyo, gaya ng tapa! Kaya tumatagal ito nang mas matagal.
copy.bis:
Mahimo ba nga modugay ang karne nang walay repridyireytor?

Oo! Ang karne mahimo tipigan pinaagi sa pag-asin ug pagpauga, sama sa tapa! Mao nga molungtad kini og mas dugay.
